test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 22 Aug 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A magnet, when moved near a coil, produces an induced potential difference in the coil. What happens when we increase the speed of the magnet near the coil?

options.text: The induced current in the coil remains the same.
The induced potential difference remains the same.
The induced potential difference in the coil decreases.
The induced potential difference in the coil increases.

solution:
The correct answer is __**the induced potential difference in the coil increases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When a magnet is moved near a coil, an induced potential difference is produced in the coil due to electromagnetic induction.
 
• **Increasing the speed of the magnet near the coil increases the rate of change of magnetic flux through the coil.**
